# Reference Notes 

Made By Abhik Biswas 

Here is a simple numerical example to show how tracking a **constant phase** allows you to follow the movement of a wave crest. 

## **The Problem** 

Suppose a water wave is described by the equation: 



<!-- Start of picture text -->
Ψ( x, t ) = 5 cos(2 x − 6 t )<br><!-- End of picture text -->

Where: 

- **Amplitude (** _A_ **):** 5 m 

- **Wavevector (** _k_ **):** 2 rad/m 

- **Angular frequency (** _ω_ **):** 6 rad/s 

- **Phase (** Φ **):** Φ( _x, t_ ) = 2 _x −_ 6 _t_ 

## **1. Condition for the Crest** 

A **crest** occurs where the wave height reaches its maximum (Ψ = +5 m). 

For 5 cos(Φ) = +5, we need cos(Φ) = 1. 

Mathematically, cos(Φ) = 1 when the phase angle is Φ = 0 **radians** (a fixed constant!). 

**2. Where is the crest at** _t_ = 0 **seconds?** 

Set the phase Φ = 0: 



<!-- Start of picture text -->
2 x 1  − 6(0) = 0 = ⇒ 2 x 1 = 0 = ⇒ x1 =  0 m<br><!-- End of picture text -->

At _t_ = 0 s, the crest is located at _x_ 1 = 0 **m** . 

Notes 

2 

## **3. Where is that SAME crest at** _t_ = 2 **seconds?** 

To stay on the **same crest** , the phase Φ **must stay locked at** 0: 



<!-- Start of picture text -->
2 x 2  − 6(2) = 0<br><!-- End of picture text -->



<!-- Start of picture text -->
2 x 2  − 12 = 0 = ⇒ 2 x 2 = 12 = ⇒ x2 =  6 m<br><!-- End of picture text -->

At _t_ = 2 s, that exact same crest has moved to _x_ 2 = 6 **m** . 

## **4. Calculate the Speed of the Crest** 

The physical speed at which the crest moved is: 



<!-- Start of picture text -->
v = ∆ x = 6 m  − 0 m =  3 m/s<br>∆ t = x t 2 2  −  − x t 1 1 2 s  − 0 s<br><!-- End of picture text -->

## **5. Compare with the Phase Velocity Formula** 

Using the standard formula _v_ phase =<sup>_<u>ω</u>_</sup> _k_<sup>:</sup> 



<!-- Start of picture text -->
v phase = 6 rad/s<br>2 rad/m =  3 m/s<br><!-- End of picture text -->

## **The Takeaway** 

1. Staying on the crest required holding the phase constant (Φ = 0). 

2. As time _t_ increased from 0 s _→_ 2 s, the position _x_ **had to increase** from 0 m _→_ 6 m to keep Φ = 0. 

3. Holding Φ = constant is simply the mathematical tool that tracks the moving peak through space!
